pr_title: Rewrite away type converting functions that do not convert types
pr_body:
When a type converting function does not actually convert the type, it can be rewritten away. This opens the door for the resulting aliasing eval to also be rewritten into a project, which removes the ReferenceAttribute, and open the door for improved optimizations.

In particular it Fixes #107716

Fixes #107716

issue_context.title: [ESQL] Difference in performance of two equivalent queries with st_centroid_agg
issue_context.body:
I have an index that contains a geo_point field. The following query takes 0.5 seconds to run:
```
from points | stats st_centroid_agg(location) 
```

But the following query takes more than 20 seconds:

```
from points | stats st_centroid_agg(TO_GEOPOINT(location)) 
```
Both queries are equivalent but the first one is reading values from doc values while the second one is reading them from _source. We can probably do better than that.

review_comments:
Hmm, why only in case of field attrs? Wouldn't this more general optimization also work?
```suggestion
                if (fa.dataType() == convert.dataType()) {
```

I only changed FieldAttribute because my primary goal was to enable lucene optimizations done by physical planning, and ReferenceAttributes that hide FieldAttributes were the main issue. Expanding to a wider scope could make sense, but also does not change performance in any way at all. The current PR makes one query 75x faster! I was already mildly concerned that my changes would have some subtle unforeseen side-effects, so did not want to widen the scope beyond what I actually needed.
